newsitem.title: POLAND: Foreign sales one of reasons for zloty fall-NBP.
newsitem.headline: Foreign sales one of reasons for zloty fall-NBP.

text.p: Foreign sales of Polish T-bills are one of several reasons behind the zloty's recent steep decline, deputy central bank president Witold Kozinski told a news conference on Monday.
He said that foreign holdings of Polish T-bills diminshed to 7.5 percent last week from 11.5 percent a month ago.
"We are watching foreign involvement in Polish T-bills very closely and their holdings have fallen from 11.5 percent a month ago to 7.5 percent last week," Kozinski said.
"It is one of the reasons for the fall of the zloty, but not the only one. I do not want to comment on the zloty's exchange rate any further," he said.

On Tuesday the zloty plummeted almost five percent to 5.25/5.65 percent below the parity rate at 1215 GMT, unhindered by the central bank on what dealers said was speculation by domestic players, with foreigners mostly on the sidelines.
